title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page, page 156 of SGA 7 Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §12.4. It is in the semistable-curve case, filed among the manuscript notes of cote 136. The 'IX' header and the typescript format identify it; the archive stamp 474 suggests it was inserted from another dossier.

Setting: C is the special fibre of a semistable curve over a discrete valuation ring (DVR). C̃ is its normalisation, and the x_i (i ∈ I) are the ordinary double points. M is the character group of the toric part of the special fibre of the Néron model of the Jacobian. By (12.4.1), M is identified with H_1 of the dual graph, i.e. ker(d: Z^I → Z^{components}).

(12.4.2) The boundary map is d(x_i) = C'_i − C''_i, which depends on an orientation of each edge.

(12.4.3) φ_{x_i}: M → Z is the i-th coordinate of M ⊂ Z^I. Reversing the orientation of edge i changes the sign of φ_{x_i} and nothing else.

(12.4.4) Hence φ_{x_i}⊗φ_{x_i} ∈ Hom(M⊗M, Z) is canonical.

(12.4.5) The sum u = Σ φ_{x_i}⊗φ_{x_i} is a canonical symmetric pairing on M. It is positive definite because it is the restriction of the standard form ΣX_i² on Z^I to the sublattice M.

Role: this is the explicit computation of Grothendieck's monodromy pairing in the curve case. Here it equals the cycle-lattice pairing of the dual graph, with all edge weights 1 at this stage; the general case weights each edge by the thickness of the double point.
errors: 'passant par i' should read 'passant par x_i' (slip).
Positivity uses that M → Z^I is injective, which holds since M = ker d. This is implicit but correct.
